‘Mini Switzerland’ in Rajshahi emerges as new tourist attraction
item.description:
A newly emerged sandbar in the Padma River is attracting growing numbers of visitors after photos and videos on social media branded the scenic spot as Rajshahi’s "Mini Switzerland".
Located in Char Khidirpur area of Paba upazila, the sandbar is locally known as Middle Char. Its white sand, green fields, grazing cattle, Kash flowers and vast stretches of the Padma have turned it into an emerging destination for nature lovers and day-trippers.
Visitors usually travel to the char from Dogor Ghat by boat, a journey that takes about 30 minutes, followed by a roughly two-kilometre walk to the main settlement. Boats have been carrying visitors throughout the day, and boatmen say passenger numbers have increased sharply in recent weeks.
“Just two weeks ago, boatmen used to spend their time sitting idle at this ghat. Suddenly, people started coming to visit the char,” said boatman Sujon Ali. He said the fare remains Tk25 per person and that the increased flow of visitors has improved their earnings.
Middle Char changes dramatically with the seasons. During the monsoon, the Padma surrounds the sandbar with water, while receding water reveals broad stretches of white sand. In autumn and winter, Kash flowers add colour to the landscape, while green vegetation and grazing livestock create a striking contrast.
The scenery is particularly attractive in the late afternoon, when sunlight reflects on the river and the changing colours of the sky appear on the water.
The term “Mini Switzerland” is not an official tourism designation. It is an informal nickname popularised by visitors and social media content creators. Although the char has long been familiar to local residents, Facebook, YouTube and TikTok videos have recently introduced it to people across Rajshahi and beyond.
Mohammad Mobasher, a ninth-grade student of Madinatul Ulum Kamil Madrasa, said he visited after watching videos online.
“I saw many videos about this char on Facebook and YouTube. I really like it here,” he said. “There is a huge field beside the vast river, and the whole area is green. Cattle are grazing across the field. We played football with our friends and went swimming in the river. Overall, we had a great time.”
Rajshahi College student Ishrat Jahan visited the char with seven friends. She said the open landscape offered a sense of freedom that was difficult to find in the city.
“It feels like opening a window to the outside world,” she said.
Despite the rising number of tourists, Middle Char remains home to a community dependent mainly on agriculture and livestock. Most houses are made of corrugated metal sheets and straw, while raised sandy paths serve as roads.
Livestock farming is an important source of income. Some herds contain between 80 and 300 animals, including cows, sheep, goats and buffaloes. Milk produced on the char is sold in Rajshahi city, including to hotels and other businesses, while some residents sell milk along the river embankment for Tk70-Tk80 per litre. Jute is another important seasonal activity.
However, the rising river level has disrupted daily life. Char Khidirpur Government Primary School has experienced declining attendance as students struggle to cross waterlogged areas. Teachers expect attendance to improve after the water recedes.
The growing tourist presence has also raised safety concerns, especially during the monsoon. Changing sandbanks, soft sand, sudden depressions and strong river currents can pose serious risks.
On August 13, Rajshahi City Corporation distributed life jackets to boatmen at the ghat and instructed them to prevent overloading and ensure passengers wear life jackets. Naval Police are also encouraging visitors to follow safety measures.
Local residents have urged tourists not to leave plastic, polythene or food packaging behind. Officials and community members believe Middle Char could become a significant tourism destination if its popularity is managed responsibly.
Improved boat safety, waste-management facilities, visitor guidelines and community-based tourism could help develop the char while protecting its natural environment. For now, the Padma, white sand, greenery and open sky continue to draw visitors seeking a brief escape from the bustle of Rajshahi city.
Rajshahi region Naval Police Superintendent Mohammad Billal Hossain said passengers were being encouraged to use life jackets.
“Many passengers are still reluctant to wear life jackets, but we are trying to convince everyone,” he said.
Harian Union ward member Shahidul Islam said the number of visitors had increased significantly after content creators began posting photographs and videos of Middle Char.
He urged visitors to refrain from throwing plastic, polythene and food packaging on the char.
Local residents and officials believe the area could become a significant tourism destination if the growing popularity is managed properly.

item.title: Alex Emon murder: 3 arrested with firearms
item.description:
RAB-2 has arrested three people, including Md Hossain Ahmed Shahrukh, the second accused in the widely discussed Alex Emon murder case in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur.
They were arrested during separate operations in the Shahbagh and Rayerbazar areas on Saturday.
RAB-2 Commander Naimul Hasan disclosed the matter at a press briefing at the unit’s Mohammadpur headquarters.
The arrestees are: Md Hossain Ahmed Shahrukh, Md Tarekuzzaman Tarek, 30, and Md Shahidul Islam, 29.
RAB said an intelligence operation found that Shahrukh, a named accused in the case, and his associates were staying in Shahbagh. A team of RAB-2 later conducted a raid there and arrested the three.
Based on information obtained during interrogation, RAB later raided a house on Haji Yunus Khan Road in Rayerbazar.
The raid yielded a foreign-made 7.65mm pistol, a magazine, a locally made revolver, two rounds of ammunition, 260 grammes of gunpowder and two samurai swords, RAB said.
Naimul Hasan said several cases had previously been filed against Shahrukh with Mohammadpur Police Station, including two for theft, attempted robbery, attempted murder and intimidation; one for murder; one under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act; and one under the Speedy Trial Act.
Tarekuzzaman Tarek also has a case filed with Mohammadpur Police Station on charges of theft, attempted murder and intimidation, RAB said.
According to RAB, 11 people have so far been arrested in the Alex Emon murder case, including six named in the FIR and five others whose identities were initially unknown. Operations are ongoing to arrest the remaining suspects.

item.title: Info minister: Govt to establish Modern Information Complex in every district, upazila
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon has said the government is constructing modern information complex in every division.
The program will also be expanded at district and upazila level, he said while inaugurating the construction work of the modern Barisal Divisional Information Complex at Ichhakathi in Kashipur of Barisal city on Sunday.
The event was organized by the Department of Mass Communication under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
The information complexes will multifaceted centers for information, knowledge, entertainment and research, he said.
“The complexes will not only be eye-catching buildings; they will serve as hubs of information, knowledge and research. The complexes will primarily function as Digital Information Service Centers, providing a wide range of digital services to the public,” he said.
Swapon said development work under the project is already underway in 26 districts. To popularize the facilities and encourage students to engage in research, promotional leaflets will be distributed to local educational institutions through the ministry, he said.
“The government’s objective is not limited to infrastructure development; rather, it aims to bring the quality of the complexes up to international standard,” he said.
To achieve this, Swapon said, both infrastructure engineering and software engineering are being given separate and equal importance.
Highlighting the technological facilities planned for the complexes, Swapon said they would feature state-of-the-art, technology-enabled cineplexes and electronic screens, with facilities for screening digital movies as well as 3D and 4D films.
Speaking as chair of the event, Secretary of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Mahbuba Farjana said the information complexes would play important role in combating misinformation and disinformation.
Barisal Divisional Commissioner Khalil Ahmed, Barisal City Corporation Administrator Advocate Bilkis Akter Jahan Shirin, spoke among others on the occasion.
In his welcome address, Project Director Moniruzzaman said the seven-storey modern Information Complex in Barisal is being constructed at a cost of Taka 17.63 crore.
Later, Deputy Project Director Rezaur Rabbi Moni presented details of the project through a multimedia presentation.

item.title: Model Ridhika Ridhi’s boyfriend sent to jail in suicide abetment case
item.description:
Model Ridhika Ridhi’s boyfriend, Hasibur Rahman, has been sent to jail in a case filed over her death at her Bashundhara Residential Area home in Dhaka. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mahbub Alam passed the order on Sunday, said Prosecution Department Sub-Inspector Kamal Hossain.
Family members found Ridhi hanging from a ceiling fan in her bedroom on Saturday morning. She was rushed to Kurmitola General Hospital where doctors declared her dead.
Ridhi’s mother Moni Begum filed a case on the same day, accusing Hasibur of abetting her daughter’s suicide.
Hasibur, who had visited Ridhi’s home that day, was arrested from the spot.
On Sunday, Vatara police Sub-Inspector Abdul Wadud, the investigating officer, produced Hasibur before the court and sought his detention in jail.
In the petition, police said preliminary interrogation and investigation had yielded sufficient evidence supporting the allegations against Hasibur. They said he had confessed to the offence and admitted his involvement during questioning.
Police also expressed concern that he might flee if released on bail.
Hasibur’s lawyer, Golam Kibria Choton, sought bail and requested a hearing on Tuesday. The court sent Hasibur to jail and fixed Tuesday for the bail hearing. Police said Ridhi had been on a video call with Hasibur when the incident occurred. Although the death initially appeared to be a suicide, investigators are probing the circumstances to determine the exact cause of death.
Ridhi, who worked as a model, also acted in several dramas, including Ekhane Manush Bikri Hoy, Bahurupi, Double Honeymoon and Sundori.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 908 as 6 more die in 24hrs
item.description:
Six children died with measles-like symptoms in 24 hours until 8am on Sunday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 908 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all six latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With this, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 809, while confirmed deaths from measles have remained the same at 99.
A total of 1021 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 142,797.
Meanwhile, 80 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 17,880.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 124,457 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 119,939 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: Family Card brings relief to some, leaves Korail slum’s poorest behind
item.description:
Ahead of the 13th parliamentary election, the BNP pledged in its election manifesto to introduce the Family Card programme to strengthen the economic security of people, particularly women.
The government launched the pilot programme on March 10 at the T&T playground in Banani, adjacent to Dhaka’s Korail slum. Under the pilot programme, selected women receive Tk 2,500 a month through mobile financial services or bank accounts.
Since then, “Family Card” has become a familiar term among Korail residents. While the programme has brought relief to some families, many of the slum’s poorest residents say they have been left out.
Residents interviewed by Dhaka Tribune alleged that some relatively well-off households received the cards, while families struggling to afford even basic food were denied the benefit.
Rasheda, Morzina among those left out
Rasheda Begum, originally from Rangpur, has lived in Korail for more than a decade. With no homestead in her village, the slum has become her last refuge. She has two children, Tabassum and Zakaria. Tabassum has a disability. Rasheda begs on the streets and in the alleys around Mohakhali to support her children. Her husband left her after their child was born with a disability.
Despite applying for a Family Card, she did not receive one.
A similar story was shared by Morzina Khatun and her son Majnu, both of whom have physical disabilities. They have no homestead in their village and have lived in Korail for around 20 years.
Unable to walk, Morzina begs while sitting on a two-wheeled cart.
Rasheda and Morzina told Dhaka Tribune that officials collected their national ID details and photographs before the pilot programme began, but they received neither cards nor payments.
They alleged that many families with relatively better incomes received cards, while those struggling to afford three meals a day were left out.
“I eat when I can beg. Otherwise, I have to go without food,” Morzina said.
Rasheda said she had contemplated suicide because of poverty but was staying alive for her helpless children. Better-off families among beneficiaries
There is a contrasting picture in Korail, with some residents who appear relatively financially secure also receiving Family Cards.
Nasima Begum is one of them. Her husband, Ashraful, works as a school van driver. Nasima has a two-storey tin-roofed house in the slum with seven rooms, which she rents out for around Tk 5,000 each, earning about Tk 35,000 a month.
“I have received four months’ payments through the Family Card. But I have not received the payments for July and August yet,” she told Dhaka Tribune.
Poorest residents demand inclusion
During a visit to Beltola Adarsh Nagar in Korail on Saturday afternoon, this correspondent found tin-roofed shacks lining narrow lanes. Most homes are so cramped that there is barely enough space to stand inside.
Women in most households work as domestic workers or in garment factories. Many families have several children. In some households, husbands do not support their families, while in others, even the combined income of both spouses is insufficient to make ends meet.
For such families, the Family Card is a much-anticipated source of support.
Under the social safety-net programme, selected families receive cash through mobile financial services. But many households living alongside beneficiaries remain excluded.
Several residents who did not receive cards told Dhaka Tribune that elderly people, widows, persons with disabilities, people suffering from chronic illnesses and families without an earning member should receive priority.
They said only a few such families had received cards, while most remained excluded.
Disabled child, jailed husband leave Sharifa struggling
Sharifa Begum lives in Beltola Adarsh Nagar and works as a domestic helper. Her son Suman has a physical disability. His grandmother looks after him while Sharifa is at work. His father is currently in jail in connection with a case.
“I have done everything short of begging at people’s feet for a Family Card, but no one helped me. My husband is in jail. Even after working in people’s homes, I cannot afford two meals a day. I cannot afford treatment for my disabled child,” Sharifa said, wiping away tears.She appealed to the government for assistance for her son.
Alecha Begum, another extremely poor resident, also did not receive a card. Her husband is ill and unable to work. She earns a living doing domestic work. “I applied for a card but did not get one. Those who are better off got cards, but we did not,” she said.
Another resident, Jharna, said, “My husband’s income is not enough to run the family. I am struggling with two children. We desperately need a card.”
Four months’ payments received, July-August dues remain
Some beneficiaries received Tk 2,500 a month from March through June under the pilot programme, but several said they have yet to receive payments for July and August.
Marium Begum told Dhaka Tribune that she had received four months’ payments through mobile banking but had not received the payments for July and August.
Sharmin Begum said, “I have not received the money for two months, July and August. I went to the office to find out what happened, but they could not give me any information.”
PM to formally launch programme in Kishoreganj
Following the pilot phase, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is scheduled to formally launch the Family Card programme in Kishoreganj on August 16. The launch is scheduled to take place at Ward 8 of Latifabad Union in Kishoreganj Sadar upazila.
Mohammad Rezaur Rahman, deputy director of the Department of Social Services, told Dhaka Tribune that the prime minister would formally launch the programme in Kishoreganj on August 16.
The programme will then be rolled out gradually across all upazilas and unions by the end of October.
Who will receive Family Cards?
Women from extremely poor, poor and low-income households will primarily be eligible for the cards, with extremely poor and poor families receiving priority during the initial phase.
Under the government guidelines, landless and homeless families, households with persons with disabilities, hijra and Bede communities, ethnic minority families and households owning up to 0.5 acres of land will receive priority.
A maximum of five members of each family will be considered for eligibility. In joint families, a separate card will be issued for every five members.

item.title: Building stronger institutions: Shafiqul Alam's role in Bangladesh's governance journey
item.description:
Corporate governance has become one of the defining themes of Bangladesh's corporate sector over the past three decades.
Regulatory reforms, expanding capital markets and growing investors’ expectations have steadily reshaped how companies are expected to operate.
Alongside these changes, a number of professionals have helped translate governance principles into practice.
Md Shafiqul Alam FCA, FCMA, FCS is one of them.
Over the past two decades, his work has spanned audit, financial reporting, governance advisory and professional education, bringing him into close engagement with the boards of directors of public and private companies, regulators and corporate leaders.
Currently serving as managing partner and CEO of Shafiqul Alam & Co., Chartered Accountants, and as council member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh (ICAB) for the 2025–2028 term, Alam has been part of the broader conversation on governance standards in Bangladesh.
The introduction of the Corporate Governance Guidelines in 2006 was one of the earliest attempts to establish structured governance expectations for listed companies.
More than a decade later, the Corporate Governance Code introduced in 2018 expanded those expectations and strengthened board oversight, with greater emphasis on independent directors, audit committees, risk management and disclosure standards.
More recently, the Financial Reporting Council's (FRC) initiative to develop a dedicated governance code for non-listed Public Interest Entities (PIEs) has drawn attention to governance practices beyond the listed sector–an area that has remained relatively less regulated despite its significant economic footprint.
These changes have also reshaped the role of directors, senior executives, finance professionals and auditors.
Issues that rarely appeared on boardroom agendas two decades ago, such as cybersecurity, ESG reporting, enterprise risk management, succession planning and board effectiveness, are now regular subjects of discussion.
As governance expectations have evolved, so too has the role of governance professionals.
Alam views corporate governance as more than regulatory compliance.
His professional work reflects the view that governance is about building institutions that are transparent, accountable and capable of sustaining long-term growth.
Good governance, he believes, should become part of an organization's culture rather than a checklist prepared for regulators.
Organizations create lasting value when transparency, ethical leadership, sound risk management and board accountability are embedded in everyday decision-making.
Alongside his professional practice, Alam has remained actively engaged in governance education and capacity building.
Those engagements have included training programs with the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC), Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), Bangladesh Institute of Capital Market (BICM) and the Bangladesh Academy for Securities Markets (BASM).
The programs have brought together directors, senior executives, company secretaries, finance professionals, auditors and market participants to examine the practical application of governance principles and evolving regulatory requirements.
The discussions focused on helping participants understand how governance principles can be applied in day-to-day business decisions rather than treated solely as compliance requirements.
Alam has also been involved in professional discussions on strengthening governance standards for non-listed public interest entities.
While listed companies are already subject to comprehensive governance requirements under the BSEC Corporate Governance Code, many non-listed public interest entities–including large financial institutions, insurers, state-owned enterprises and other significant players–manage substantial public resources without being covered by a dedicated governance framework.
Strengthening governance within these entities, he argues, can improve accountability, enhance financial reporting quality, protect lenders and other stakeholders, and reinforce confidence across the broader financial system.
For Alam, strengthening governance in these entities is ultimately about strengthening the institutions that underpin Bangladesh's economy.
As businesses become larger, more technology-driven and increasingly connected to international markets, governance frameworks must adapt to address emerging issues such as enterprise risk management, cybersecurity, ESG reporting, succession planning and board effectiveness.
Sustainable governance depends not only on well-designed regulations but also on competent professionals capable of implementing those regulations effectively.
Over the years, Alam's work with chartered accountants, company secretaries, finance executives, internal auditors and board members has focused on promoting higher professional standards and encouraging continuous learning.
His work across audit, assurance, financial reporting and board advisory has given him practical exposure to governance practices across a wide range of companies.
This experience has reinforced his view that governance cannot be reduced to documentation alone–effective governance ultimately depends on leadership, ethical decision-making and institutional culture.
Rather than viewing governance as an obstacle to entrepreneurship, he presents it as a framework that enables businesses to grow sustainably while protecting the interests of investors, lenders, employees and society.
Bangladesh's governance journey remains a work in progress. As regulatory expectations continue to evolve and businesses face increasingly complex risks, governance is likely to remain central to corporate decision-making.
Professionals involved in policy, education and advisory services will continue to shape that transition.
Md Shafiqul Alam's career reflects one part of that broader institutional story.

item.title: Tk 1.21C robbery from PM’s cousin’s petrol pump: Five arrested
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) has arrested five people over the robbery of Tk 1.21 crore from a petrol pump in Uttara, allegedly linked to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s maternal cousin Tasin Akhtar Haque.
Police also recovered RAB-marked vests, fake identity cards, firearms and other equipment allegedly used in the robbery. The suspected mastermind remains at large.
The arrestees are: Md Ilias Shikdar, 36, Jafar, 36, Md Rabiul Islam alias Rubel, 34, Mintu Rari, 23, and Sagar Baroi, 40.
Additional Police Commissioner (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre on Saturday.
He said four employees of DL Filling Station were carrying Tk 1.21 crore to a bank around 10:30am on August 9 when a group of motorcycle-borne robbers intercepted them near Crown Plaza on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Road.
The robbers allegedly threatened and assaulted them with firearms and machetes before fleeing with the money.
Following the incident, the DB and Uttara Crime Division launched a joint investigation. Acting on intelligence, police arrested Ilias Shikdar and Jafar in Siddhirganj, Narayanganj.
Police later recovered three RAB-marked vests, two caps, fake RAB identity cards, number plates, walkie-talkies, handcuffs, two 7.65mm pistols, three magazines and six rounds of ammunition from Ilias’s rented home in Bandar.
Rubel and Mintu were subsequently arrested in Matuail and Kazlarpar, respectively. Police recovered Tk 3 lakh in stolen cash from Rubel’s residence, while a raid on Mintu’s home yielded four RAB-marked vests, fake RAB IDs, number plates, walkie-talkies, handcuffs, two pistols, three magazines and 15 rounds of ammunition.
Based on information provided by Rubel and Mintu, police arrested Sagar from his rented home in Postogola and recovered Tk 9 lakh in stolen cash. Shafiqul Islam said the stolen money was divided among the gang, with the masterminds taking larger shares and others receiving portions for providing logistical support. Sagar received Tk 9 lakh but had not spent it, he added.
The DB chief said ballistic checks showed that the recovered firearms were not weapons looted from police but had been illegally acquired.
He said the mastermind remains at large and that investigators had found no prior personal connection between the suspect and the victim.
According to police, the gang targeted the petrol pump after learning that several days’ cash had accumulated because banks were closed during the holidays. The group allegedly planned the robbery knowing the money would be deposited once the banks reopened.
Police said efforts are underway to arrest the remaining suspects and recover the rest of the stolen money.

item.title: Bangladesh, Kosovo reaffirm strong opposition to all forms of transnational crimes
item.description:
Recognizing their common commitment to peace, stability, and international security, Bangladesh and Kosovo have reaffirmed their strong opposition to terrorism, violent extremism, and all forms of transnational crime.
They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the friendly relations between the two countries on the basis of mutual respect, shared values, common interests, and the principles of international law.
The issues of mutual interest were discussed at the second Foreign Office Consultations between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora of the Republic of Kosovo held in Prishtina recently.
The Bangladeshi delegation was led by Dr M Nazrul Islam, secretary (Bilateral – East & West) of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while the Kosovar delegation was led by Ilir Muçaj, secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Diaspora.
The two sides acknowledged the significant untapped potential for expanding bilateral cooperation in the fields of trade, investment, education, agriculture, information and communication technology, tourism, labour mobility, and people-to-people exchanges.
They agreed to continue working closely to fully utilise the complementarities of their respective economies for mutual benefit.
The two sides reviewed the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and expressed satisfaction with the steady progress achieved since the establishment of diplomatic relations, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Both sides welcomed the bilateral instruments concluded thus far and emphasized their importance in strengthening institutional cooperation.
They agreed that bilateral relations would be further enhanced through the early conclusion of the agreements currently under negotiation, particularly those related to economic cooperation, the avoidance of double taxation, and other mutually beneficial areas.
The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing cooperation at both the bilateral and multilateral levels and agreed to continue close coordination and consultation in regional and international organizations on issues of mutual interest.
The Kosovo side highly appreciated Bangladesh's longstanding contribution to United Nations peacekeeping operations and expressed its sincere gratitude to the members of the Bangladesh to the UN Peace-Keeping Forces who served in Kosovo.
The Bangladeshi side welcomed Kosovo's growing participation in international and regional organizations and initiatives and expressed its support for Kosovo's continued integration into international organizations, conventions, and multilateral mechanisms as an equal participant.
The Kosovo side commended Bangladesh for its humanitarian response to the Rohingya refugee crisis and expressed its support for Bangladesh's efforts aimed at ensuring the safe, voluntary, dignified, and sustainable repatriation of the displaced Rohingya population to Rakhine State in Myanmar.
The Kosovo side also underlined the importance of sustained engagement by the international community to facilitate a durable solution to the crisis.
The two sides recognized the growing demand for labour mobility and underlined the importance of establishing a structured framework for the recruitment and employment of Bangladeshi workers in Kosovo.
They agreed to explore the possibility of developing government-to-government (G2G) cooperation mechanisms that would ensure transparent, orderly, and mutually beneficial labour migration.
The two sides emphasized the importance of maintaining regular Foreign Office Consultations as an effective mechanism for strengthening bilateral cooperation, reviewing progress, and identifying new areas of collaboration.
They agreed to hold the third Foreign Office Consultations in Dhaka during 2027 at a mutually convenient date.
The consultations were held in a constructive atmosphere, reflecting the excellent relations between the Republic of Kosovo and the People's Republic of Bangladesh and their shared commitment to further deepening bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Muddy road causes suffering for Madhupur people
item.description:
A three-kilometre muddy road in Madhupur upazila of Tangail is causing immense suffering for local residents, particularly during the monsoon.
The road, stretching from Pichila Ghona to Momin Ara along the border areas of Ausnara and Mahishmara unions, is yet to be paved or widened despite its importance to the local community.
During the rainy season, several sections of the road become waterlogged and muddy, making it difficult for vehicles and pedestrians to move. The poor condition also severely disrupts the transportation of agricultural produce to markets, leaving farmers to suffer.
Locals said agricultural land and various establishments have developed on both sides of the road. Madhupur’s famous pineapples and other agricultural products are transported to markets using this route. But even a light shower leaves parts of the road submerged and covered in mud, making travel extremely difficult.
Students, patients, traders and pedestrians are among those who face difficulties due to the road’s dilapidated condition. Farmers are particularly affected as they struggle to take their produce to market in time and at reasonable transportation costs.
Abu Hanif, a resident of Haldia village, said the road is extremely important for people in the area. “During the rainy season, the road becomes so bad that even walking becomes difficult. It should be paved without further delay,” he said.
Another resident, Ainal Haque, said a large number of people use the road every day. Farmers, in particular, face serious problems while transporting pineapples and other crops to markets. “If the road is improved, transportation of agricultural products will become easier, and farmers will have a better chance of getting fair prices,” he said.
A resident, Chan Mia, said locals have been demanding repairs for years. “The suffering increases several times once the rainy season begins. If the road is permanently paved, the long-standing problems of the people will be greatly reduced,” he said.
Madhupur Upazila Engineer Rafiqul Islam Bhuiyan said the road from Pichila Ghona to Momin Ara has been sent for inclusion in the government gazette. “Once the road is assigned an ID number and funds are allocated, work will begin,” he said.

All filling stations shut down in Brahmanbaria amid gas crisis
item.description:
All CNG filling stations in Brahmanbaria have been shut down due to a severe gas shortage, causing widespread suffering for passengers and transport workers. Gas supply to the stations was completely suspended from Thursday night, with no clear indication of when services will resume.
According to sources, Bakhrabad Gas Distribution Company Limited had been supplying gas to five filling stations in the district at a reduced rate since Wednesday. Before the crisis, the stations received around 50,000 cubic metres of gas daily, although demand was nearly double that amount.
For more than two weeks, gas pressure at the stations had remained unusually low. Against the normal pressure of 15 PSI, the stations were receiving only 2-3 PSI. Supply was reduced further on Wednesday before being completely suspended on Thursday night.
The shutdown has severely affected CNG-powered vehicles. Many CNG auto-rickshaw drivers have switched to LPG cylinders, resulting in higher fares. Passenger numbers have also fallen as fewer vehicles are operating on roads and highways.
Farid Mia, a passenger, said he waited for an hour at Kumarshil intersection for a CNG auto-rickshaw to travel to Bishwa Road. The driver initially demanded Tk 80, although the regular fare is Tk 40. After bargaining, they agreed on Tk 70.
Rafik Mia, a driver, said the regular fare from Kumarshil intersection to Sarail-Bishwa Road is Tk 50. He had been charging Tk 70 amid the gas shortage and now charges Tk 90 after switching to LPG.
Md Monayem Mia, manager of Khwaja Garib-e-Nawaz Filling Station in Sarail, said the station was forced to close due to the lack of gas. He said Bakhrabad Gas Distribution officials indicated that supply might resume on Sunday or Monday.
Md Shafiqul Haque, deputy general manager of Bakhrabad Gas Distribution's Brahmanbaria office, attributed the crisis to an LNG shortage. He said authorities could not confirm when the situation would improve, though they hoped the crisis would end soon.

item.title: Load shedding halves production at Gopalganj BSCIC Industrial Estate
item.description:
Frequent load shedding has cut industrial production by nearly half at Gopalganj BSCIC Industrial Estate, where factories are experiencing around five hours of power outages during the 11-hour working period each day.
Production at the estate normally runs from 9:00 am to 8:00 pm. As most factories depend heavily on electricity, frequent outages are disrupting production, while owners still have to pay workers their full wages. As a result, industrial units are incurring significant losses, with plastic factories reportedly bearing the brunt.
According to the Executive Engineer’s Office of West Zone Power Distribution Company (WZPDCL) in Gopalganj, the BSCIC feeder has a daily demand of around 2 megawatts, while only 1-1.25 megawatts is being supplied.
Sujan Das, industrial estate officer of Gopalganj BSCIC, said the estate has 74 industrial plots, of which 61 currently have operational units. These include wooden and steel furniture factories, pulse mills, automobile and engineering workshops, polymer industries, oil mills, puffed-rice and sanitary-product manufacturing units.
He said frequent load shedding had reduced production across the estate, while voltage fluctuations were damaging machinery. Factory owners were also paying workers despite production remaining suspended. “We have started working with the relevant authorities to ensure uninterrupted power supply to the BSCIC industrial estate,” he added.
Kazi Hasan, director of Khan Industries, which operates three plastic-related units, said its machines require about two hours to heat up before production can begin. However, electricity often goes off and returns every hour.
“When the power goes out, the machine temperature drops to zero. Raw materials are damaged inside the machines, workers remain idle and production stops. This causes losses on three fronts,” he said.
Hasan said the company’s polymer units had suffered the most. A machine screw worth around Tk 250,000 was damaged and will have to be imported from China, taking about 15 days.
Imam Hasan, director of Sharif Furniture, said voltage fluctuations had caused losses of around Tk 300,000. He said five to six hours of load shedding during the factory’s 11-hour working period had reduced production to about 45%.
“Workers sit idle during outages, but we still have to pay them. Furniture supplies to showrooms have also declined alarmingly,” he said, demanding uninterrupted daytime power.
Bidhan Biswas, proprietor of Moni Engineering Workshop, said hourly outages had severely disrupted production of rice-husking machines and agricultural equipment. Production during the first 12 days of this month had fallen by half.
Lutfar Rahman Luthu, proprietor of Lutfar Rahman Pulses Mill, said power shortages had reduced production and prevented the mill from meeting market demand.
Mohammad Iqbal Hossain, owner of Gopalganj Motors, said electricity was essential for automobile servicing. “Without electricity, almost everything at the BSCIC estate comes to a standstill,” he said.
Mohammad Moin Uddin, executive engineer of WZPDCL’s Gopalganj town electricity supply office, said the town’s nine feeders have a combined demand of 18 megawatts, while only 8 to 9 megawatts are supplied from the national grid.
He said the power situation had started improving on Thursday and assured that special attention would be given to the BSCIC feeder.

item.title: 5 arrested for running online betting, gambling ring
item.description:
The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has arrested five members of an organised ring allegedly involved in operating online betting and gambling platforms.
The arrested suspects are: Rafiqul Islam, 46, Md Sohel, 37, Md Shafiqul Islam, 27, Md Rubel Molla, 33, and Ayub Hossain Ripon, 48. All are from Narsingdi.
The CID’s Cyber Police Centre (CPC) arrested them in separate raids across Narsingdi between Wednesday evening and Thursday.
Police recovered nine mobile phones, 20 SIM cards, cheque books from several banks and other evidence from their possession.
Jasim Uddin Khan, special superintendent of police (media) at the CID, said preliminary questioning indicated the suspects’ links to an organised online betting and gambling network.
“Initial investigations suggest that an organised group operating both in Bangladesh and abroad has been running online betting and gambling websites under various names for a long time,” he said.
The group allegedly arranged betting and gambling for money around international cricket, football and other sporting events, while promoting the activities through social media and other online platforms, Jasim Uddin Khan said.
The CID urged the public to refrain from online gambling and betting activities.

item.title: DMP takes zero-tolerance stance on drugs, snatching
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed has directed police to adopt a zero-tolerance approach to drug-related crimes, take effective measures to prevent illegal activities at hotels and spa centres, and maintain round-the-clock surveillance in snatching-prone areas.
He gave the directives at the monthly crime review meeting for July 2026, held at the Bangladesh Police Auditorium in Rajarbagh in the capital on Thursday. The DMP commissioner instructed police to strengthen intelligence activities alongside regular drives against drug dealers and others involved in drug-related crimes.
He also directed officials concerned to take necessary measures to prevent illegal activities at hotels and spa centres within their respective police station areas. “If information about such activities is received, immediate legal action should be taken while maintaining regular surveillance,” he said.
To prevent snatching, Mosleh Uddin instructed the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit and Detective Branch (DB) to maintain round-the-clock field presence in coordination with the Crime Division after identifying snatching-prone areas.
He also ordered stronger intelligence surveillance, patrols and operations in those areas and directed the units concerned to work in coordination to bring the criminals to justice.
The DMP chief further asked the officers-in-charge of the relevant police stations and senior officials of the Crime Division to visit the scene of every crime. He stressed the importance of visiting crime scenes in person, collecting necessary evidence and properly examining the circumstances surrounding incidents to establish the facts and make investigations more effective.
Mosleh Uddin also directed field-level police officials to discharge their duties with the highest professionalism, responsibility and dedication to control crime and ensure the safety of city residents.

item.title: JMB member arrested in Savar sent to court
item.description:
Police sent an alleged member of banned militant outfit JMB to court on Thursday, seeking a 10-day remand in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act.
The accused, identified as Mohammad Arif, 26, was arrested by members of the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit from Hemayetpur in Savar on Tuesday. He was produced before the court from Savar Model Police Station around noon on Thursday.
According to police, several bombs were recovered from a bag in Arif’s possession at the time of his arrest. Later, based on information provided by him, police raided his rented residence in South Shyampur, Hemayetpur.
During the raid, police recovered several powerful bombs, cocktails and a large quantity of materials allegedly used to make explosives.
Police subsequently filed a case at Savar Model Police Station under the Anti-Terrorism Act, naming six people, including Arif, and several unidentified others as accused.
According to the case statement, the accused are members of the banned New JMB and had gathered in the Savar area with explosives to carry out acts of sabotage.
The statement also alleged that they supported the ideology of the banned organisation and were involved in activities aimed at creating public panic, threatening public safety and national sovereignty, and attempting to attack law enforcement personnel.
The other named accused are currently absconding, police said.
Savar Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Saiful Alam said Arif was sent to court with a 10-day remand plea.

item.title: Fakhrul’s presidential nomination sparks celebrations in Thakurgaon
item.description:
Thakurgaon, the birthplace of BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, erupted in celebration after reports that he had been finalized as the party’s candidate for Bangladesh’s 23rd presidential election.
Following a high-level BNP meeting on Thursday, news of Fakhrul’s nomination quickly spread across the district. Party activists and local residents gathered at the BNP office and his ancestral home in Kalibari. Supporters organized celebratory processions, distributed sweets and exchanged greetings, turning parts of the town into a festive scene.
Fakhrul became involved in politics as a student at Dhaka University. He later worked as a college teacher before entering local politics and being elected chairman of Thakurgaon Municipality. He subsequently served as a member of parliament, state minister and full minister.
Over more than a decade of political turbulence, Fakhrul played a significant role in keeping the BNP organized and united. His political career also included periods of imprisonment amid the party’s prolonged political struggles.
Residents described his nomination as a major achievement not only for Thakurgaon but also for the wider northern region.
Prof Abu Bakar Siddique, former principal of Thakurgaon Government Women’s College, described Fakhrul as one of the region’s most distinguished figures. He expressed hope that development initiatives for Thakurgaon would receive greater momentum if Fakhrul assumes the presidency.
Dr ABM Khairul Kabir, president of the Thakurgaon chapter of the Bangladesh Medical Association and a former director of Dinajpur Medical College Hospital, said Fakhrul’s achievement was a source of pride for the entire northern region.
District BNP President Mirza Faisal Amin said the family was deeply moved, calling the nomination recognition of Fakhrul’s lifelong sacrifice, dedication and integrity.
Residents expressed hope that, if elected president, Fakhrul would strengthen democratic institutions and help reflect the hopes and aspirations of ordinary citizens.

item.title: CUET declares campus ponds, ditches hazardous after 3 student drownings
item.description:
Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) has declared all campus ponds and ditches hazardous and banned students from bathing or swimming in them following the drowning of three students.
The directive was issued in a notice signed by Professor Saiful Islam, director of the Directorate of Students’ Welfare, on Thursday.
The notice said all campus ponds had been declared hazardous in the interest of students’ safety. Until further notice, entering, swimming or otherwise going into any campus pond is strictly prohibited.
Violators will be considered to have breached university discipline and face disciplinary action under the university’s rules, the notice said.
CUET currently has two ponds and several ditches on its campus. The decision came after three students drowned in one of the ponds in recent weeks.
On Wednesday, second-year students Chomok Dutta of the Computer Science and Engineering Department and Shanto Deb of the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department drowned while bathing in the pond.
Earlier, on July 28, fourth-year Mechanical Engineering student Arnab Saha drowned in the same pond.
According to CUET sources, Shanto and Arnab had entered the pond beside Kazi Nazrul Islam Hall to bathe with friends. They were submerged at one point and later rescued and taken to hospital, where doctors declared them dead.
The latest deaths occurred just two weeks after Arnab’s drowning, leaving the university community in mourning once again.

item.title: Fertilizer sales irregularities grip Rajshahi, farmers protest
item.description:
Farmers across the Rajshahi region are struggling to buy subsidised fertiliser at government-fixed prices, amid allegations of hoarding, diversion and an organised syndicate involving dealers and unauthorised retailers.
The crisis comes as Aman planting is underway, raising concerns among farmers that delays in getting fertiliser could affect crop yields.
Farmers allege that some dealers sell fertiliser allocation orders to black-market traders even before receiving supplies. Others reportedly sell fertiliser directly to retailers from warehouses instead of distributing it through designated outlets. There are also allegations that fertiliser allocated to one district or upazila is being diverted to another.
During visits to several rural areas of Rajshahi, most authorised dealers were found without subsidised fertiliser, while nearby retail shops were selling the same products at significantly higher prices.
Under government-fixed rates, a 50kg bag of triple super phosphate (TSP) costs Tk1,350 and a bag of diammonium phosphate (DAP) Tk1,050. Farmers, however, said they were paying Tk1,700–1,800 for TSP and around Tk1,600 for DAP because of shortages at authorised outlets.
“I have a farmer’s card. I went to authorised dealers several times but could not buy fertiliser,” said Russel Hossain, a farmer from Baraikuri village in Paba upazila.
“Fertiliser is not available at the government-fixed price. But if you are willing to pay more, there is no shortage.”
At M/s Haque & Sons Enterprise, an authorised Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) dealer at Nowhata Bazar in Paba, no subsidised fertiliser was available during the visit.
Dealer Abdul Haque said he supplies fertiliser to several thousand farmers across 42 mouzas.
“In July, I received only 22 bags of TSP, 70 bags of MOP and 110 bags of DAP. The supplies were exhausted within two or three days,” he said.
An employee of Tasnim Enterprise, another authorised dealer, also said the shop’s fertiliser stock had run out. However, shop owner Fazlur Rahman later said fertiliser was available and claimed the employee had provided incorrect information.
At a nearby retail shop, an employee offered to sell a 50kg bag of DAP for Tk1,600, Tk550 above the government-fixed price. He said the shop collected fertiliser from various sources and claimed subsidised fertiliser passed through three or four middlemen before reaching retailers.
Farmers have long alleged that a syndicate involving dishonest dealers, unauthorised retailers and officials responsible for monitoring fertiliser distribution is controlling the market.
Several farmers, speaking on condition of anonymity, alleged that field-level agricultural officials were involved in the network. They also claimed that hundreds of unauthorised fertiliser retailers were operating as part of the system.
Sajedur Rahman, a farmer from Chhoto Palashi village in Rishikul Union of Tanore, said farmers could not find fertiliser at government-fixed prices.
“When we go to the dealers, they say there is no fertiliser. We are forced to buy from high-priced retail shops,” he said.
Farmers in Palashi said TSP was selling for Tk1,700–1,800 per bag, while DAP was available for around Tk1,600. MOP, officially priced at Tk1,050, was reportedly being sold for about Tk500 more.
Despite the allegations, officials said they had not received complaints about a fertiliser shortage.
Azizur Rahman, deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Rajshahi division, said, “We have not received any complaints from farmers about a fertiliser shortage. Aman planting is underway everywhere, and agricultural officials are advising farmers.”
Kazi Shahidul Islam, Rajshahi district administrator and chairman of the district fertiliser distribution committee, said he had not received complaints about higher prices but promised to investigate.
According to Agriculture Ministry data, Rajshahi received higher allocations of TSP, DAP and MOP in July and August this year than during the same period in 2025.
The combined allocation rose from 5,876 tonnes in July 2025 to 7,033 tonnes in July 2026. August allocations also increased, with TSP rising from 1,430 tonnes to 1,511 tonnes, DAP from 2,404 tonnes to 2,647 tonnes and MOP from 1,709 tonnes to 1,760 tonnes.
Nasir Uddin, assistant director (fertiliser) at the BADC Rajshahi office, said the agency was distributing fertiliser according to the quantities approved by the Agriculture Ministry. He added that seasonal demand had increased because some farmers were applying fertiliser beyond recommended doses.
The Rajshahi agricultural region, comprising Rajshahi, Natore, Naogaon and Chapainawabganj, has set a target of cultivating Aman rice on 410,000 hectares. About 40% of the targeted area had been planted as of Wednesday.
Meanwhile, farmers in Chapainawabganj’s Gomastapur upazila staged a protest on Wednesday after failing to obtain adequate fertiliser from dealers.
Farmers from Rahonpur Union gathered at the upazila parishad premises and later met Upazila Nirbahi Officer Zillur Rahman.
They said fertiliser was unavailable during a critical stage of Aman cultivation and warned that delays could reduce crop yields.
Gomastapur Upazila Agriculture Officer Saklain Hossain said officials were monitoring the supply situation and would take action if problems were found.
UNO Zillur Rahman said necessary measures were being taken to ensure farmers received fertiliser at government-fixed prices. He warned that legal action would be taken against anyone found selling fertiliser above the fixed price, hoarding supplies to create an artificial shortage, or harassing farmers.

Strong assurances received on renewal of Ganges Water Sharing Treaty
item.description:
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Water Resources was informed on Thursday that strong assurances have been received regarding the renewal of the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty between Bangladesh and India, commonly known as the Farakka Treaty.
The committee was also informed that the main implementation work of the Teesta Master Plan is expected to begin next year.
The first meeting of the committee on the Ministry was held at the National Parliament with committee chairman Mohammad Shofiqul Haque Milon MP presiding.
The committee discussed various initiatives including advance preparaFtions to prevent river erosion and tree plantation programs.
The meeting was informed that the Padma Barrage Project has already been approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC).
A presentation was made before the committee on the overall activities of the Ministry of Water Resources including ongoing development programs, project progress, implementation periods and allocations.
According to the presentation, 93 development projects are currently being implemented under the ministry. A total of Tk 7,832.80 crore has been allocated for these projects in the 2026-27 fiscal year.
The committee called for completing the development projects within their stipulated timelines, ensuring proper and efficient use of allocated funds and taking more effective measures to improve public services.
The Ganges Water Sharing Treaty was signed by Bangladesh and India on Dec 12, 1996 for 30 years and is due to expire in December 2026.
The treaty provides for sharing Ganges water at India’s Farakka Barrage during the dry season from Jan 1 to May 31 each year on the basis of a 10-day schedule.
Under the agreement, when the flow is 70,000 cusecs or less, Bangladesh and India receive 50 percent each. If the flow is between 70,000 and 75,000 cusecs, Bangladesh receives 35,000 cusecs and India gets the remainder. When the flow is 75,000 cusecs or more, India receives 40,000 cusecs and Bangladesh gets the remainder.
With the treaty approaching expiry, its renewal has emerged as a key water-sharing issue between the two countries amid concerns over declining dry-season flows, climate change, rising water demand and downstream ecological impacts.

item.description:
Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) on Thursday submitted the nomination paper on behalf of its Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir for the presidential election.
A BNP delegation led by its Standing Committee Member Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan submitted the nomination paper to Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) A M M Nasir Uddin, the Chief Election Officer for the presidential election, at the Election Building in the city's Agargaon.
BNP Standing Committee Member and Narsingdi-2 constituency lawmaker Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan proposed Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as a presidential candidate in the nomination paper, while BNP Standing Committee Member and Dhaka-3 constituency lawmaker Gayeshwar Chandra Roy supported it.
Earlier on Thursday, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman formally announced Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as the BNP candidate for the presidency at a meeting of the party's Standing Committee.
The prime minister proposed Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir's name for the presidential nomination, and the Standing Committee members unanimously approved the proposal.
The meeting was held today at the meeting room of the Cabinet Division at the Prime Minister's Office in Bangladesh Secretariat.
On August 9, Chief Whip of the Parliament Nurul Islam Moni and BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi collected the nomination paper from the office of the Chief Election Officer.
Earlier, the Election Commission (EC) announced the schedule for the presidential election on August 6. According to the schedule, August 13 was set as the date for submission of nomination papers, while voting will be held on August 20.

item.title: PM to attend ‘Rhidoye Dhaka 416’ event at Lalbagh Aug 29
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will attend “Rhidoye Dhaka 416,” the final event marking 416 years of historic Dhaka, at Lalbagh Fort in the capital on August 29.
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Abdus Salam announced the details at a press conference at Nagar Bhaban on Thursday.
He said the 416th anniversary of historic Dhaka will be celebrated through a range of colorful programs highlighting the city’s rich history and culture.
The special celebration has been organized under the theme “Festival, Pride and Responsibility.”
“The event is being organized with the expectation of reviving Dhaka’s heritage. When people live with Dhaka in their hearts, they will also develop a sense of responsibility to keep the city clean,” Salam said.
He said various programs will be held at different locations across the capital until September 5 as part of the celebrations.
Final event at Lalbagh Fort
The final event will begin at 4pm on August 29 at Lalbagh Fort, the DSCC administrator said.
“Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has kindly agreed to attend the event. The LGRD state minister and the administrator of Dhaka North City Corporation will also be present,” he said.
The event will feature dance performances by children, an exhibition of inventions by young scientists and an exhibition of books written about Dhaka.
There will also be stalls showcasing famous foods from Old Dhaka.
The prime minister will plant a tree and visit Lalbagh Fort during the event. He will inaugurate the program through the release of festoons and balloons, followed by the release of pigeons.
A traditional kite festival celebrating the heritage of Old Dhaka will also be inaugurated at the venue.
The special “Clean Dhaka, Green Dhaka” and mosquito-control campaigns will also be launched on the occasion and subsequently carried out in every ward, Salam said.
A documentary titled “Rhidoye Dhaka” will be screened at the event, while a commemorative book on Dhaka will also be unveiled.
The organizers also hope to unveil a commemorative postage stamp marking Dhaka Day, subject to approval from the relevant ministry.
The celebrations will conclude with a light-and-sound show and a cultural program after a short break, Salam said.

item.title: Four killed as bus collides with leguna in Cox’s Bazar
item.description:
Four people were killed and five others injured after a bus collided head-on with a leguna (Mahindra) in Chakaria upazila of Cox’s Bazar on Thursday morning.
The accident occurred around 6:30am near the Baitul Mamur Jame Mosque area in Nayapara of Khutakhali Union on the Chittagong-Cox’s Bazar Highway, said SI Mohammad Shamsuzzaman of Malumghat Highway Police Station.
The deceased were identified as Mohammad Jasim Uddin, of Segunbagicha village in Khutakhali; Mohammad Shahed, of Fulchhari Shiapara; Mohammad Rafique, of West Gajalia village in Eidgaon; and Mohammad Ziaul Haque, of Notun Office area in the same upazila.
Shahed, Rafique and Ziaul died while undergoing treatment at Cox’s Bazar District Sadar Hospital, while Jasim died at Malumghat Christian Memorial Hospital in the afternoon.
The injured are Syed Alam, his son Mohammad Sarwar, Ziaul Haque, Mohammad Delwar Hossain, and Syed Karim. They were taken to the two hospitals for treatment. Three of the injured were reported to be in critical condition.
According to police and local residents, a Lal Shobuj Paribahan bus was travelling to Cox’s Bazar from Noakhali Sadar, while the leguna was carrying passengers from Eidgaon to Chakaria. The vehicles collided head-on after reaching Nayapara in Khutakhali.
The impact left the leguna badly mangled. Locals rescued the injured and took them to nearby hospitals.
SI Shamsuzzaman said the accident occurred amid heavy rain early in the morning. Police later used a crane to remove the damaged vehicles from the highway, and traffic returned to normal about an hour later.
Police said legal procedures would be completed before the bodies are handed over to the victims’ families.

item.title: Govt moves to formulate policy on battery-run rickshaws
item.description:
The government has taken an initiative to formulate a policy for managing battery-operated rickshaws in city corporation, municipality, upazila and union parishad areas.
A discussion on the operation of three-wheeled low-speed battery-run rickshaws, commonly known as e-rickshaws, was held at the conference room of the Local Government Ministry at Bangladesh Secretariat here on Thursday.
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam presided over the meeting.
The meeting discussed the measures to effectively manage the battery-run rickshaws in light of urban management, traffic discipline, road safety and existing realities. Representatives of relevant stakeholders also presented various opinions and recommendations.
Mir Shahe Alam said a policy for managing e-rickshaws is being formulated in accordance with the Local Government (City Corporation) Act, 2009 and the Local Government (City Corporation) (Amendment) Act,20 26.
He said effective implementation of the policy would play an important role in controlling traffic congestion, maintaining traffic discipline and ensuring road safety in the cities.
The government authorities would generate revenue for the government exchequer.
The minister further said that, to achieve these objectives, steps would be taken to amend existing regulations and make them time-befitting with a view to establishing a coordinated licensing authority for city corporations, municipalities, upazilas and union councils.
It may be mentioned that relevant provisions and schedules of the Local Government (City Corporation) (Amendment) Act, 2026 have already been amended to create scope for registering battery-operated rickshaws and issuing licenses to their drivers in city corporation areas.
Earlier, on December 14, 2025, the local government division issued the “Rules on the Operation of Three-Wheeled Low-Speed Battery-Operated Rickshaws (E-Rickshaws) in City Corporation areas, 2025” to regulate e-rickshaw operations in city corporation areas. The rules were published in the gazette on December 17, 2025.
At the meeting, Prof Dr Md Hadiuzzaman of the Department of Civil Engineering at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Burt) provided expert opinions on the issue.
Among others, Dhaka South City Corporation Administrator freedom fighter Md Abdus Salam, Dhaka North City Corporation Administrator Md Shafiqul Islam Khan, Local Government Division Secretary Md Shahidul Hasan, DNCC Chief Executive Officer Muhammad Asaduzzaman, DSCC Chief Executive Officer Md Khaibar Rahman and Additional Commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (Traffic) Md Anisur Rahman attended the meeting.
Senior officials from the ministry and the city corporations concerned were also present.

item.title: Speakers call for action to implement National Urban Policy 2025
item.description:
With more than one-third of Bangladesh’s population living in urban areas and cities contributing nearly 65% of GDP, speakers on Thursday called for coordinated action to implement the National Urban Policy 2025 and translate its commitments into more livable, inclusive and climate-resilient cities.
The call came at the National Dissemination Workshop on National Urban Policy 2025, jointly organized by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Local Government Division (LGD), with support from the UK government, at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre (BCFCC) in Dhaka.
The workshop aimed to disseminate the National Urban Policy 2025 among stakeholders and gather recommendations for drafting its implementation action plan.
The event brought together representatives from government ministries and agencies, local government institutions, development partners, academia, research institutions and the urban development community.
The government approved the country’s first National Urban Policy 2025 as a national framework for more planned, inclusive, sustainable and climate-resilient urban development.
Speaking at the workshop, Md Mahmud Ali, director (additional secretary) of the Urban Development Directorate, said urban development cannot be the responsibility of a single ministry and requires coordination across sectors, with active participation from ministries, public and private institutions, development authorities, academia, professionals and urban residents.
Md Samsul Islam, joint secretary of the Local Government Division, stressed that the next priority is to move from policy to implementation.
“We want the National Urban Policy 2025 to go beyond being a policy document and become an effective tool for real change in urban planning, management, infrastructure development and service delivery,” he said.
Tanvir Mahmud, senior governance specialist at UNDP Bangladesh, said implementation at the local level would ultimately determine the policy’s impact.
“The real success of the National Urban Policy will depend on how effectively it is applied in our cities. National policy directions need to connect with local realities, local capacities and local priorities,” he said.
He added that government ownership should remain at the centre of implementation, while development partners could support the process through technical knowledge, evidence, innovation, capacity development and partnerships.
The National Urban Policy 2025 was developed under the leadership of the Local Government Division, with contributions from an inter-ministerial committee and relevant government institutions, including the Public Works Department, Ministry of Planning, and Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. UNDP provided technical support with assistance from the UK government.
Earlier, Professor Dr Shakil Akther of the Department of Urban and Regional Planning at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology presented the National Urban Policy 2025, followed by an open discussion on its implementation.
Among others, Nathaniel Smith, team leader for climate and environment at the British High Commission; Amit Datta Roy, urban specialist at the Asian Development Bank; Dr Fawzia Farzana, professor at the Department of Urban and Regional Planning at Khulna University; and Yugesh Pradhanang of UNDP spoke at the workshop.

item.title: Madrasa student’s death: Teacher placed on 3-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Thursday placed Hafiz Md Zakaria, 35, one of two teachers arrested over the death of a child student at Rowazatul Ulum Hafizia Nurani Madrasa in Rayerbagh’s Jorakhamba area, on a three-day remand.
The court did not hear the remand plea against Hafiz Md Zubayer Ahmed, 20, after his lawyer claimed he was a minor. The court fixed August 18 to hear the matter.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mahbub Alam passed the order on Thursday, said Abdus Sabur, a sub-inspector of the prosecution department.
After the hearing, relatives of the deceased allegedly attacked the accused as police were taking them to jail from the court premises.
The body of Naim Sheikh, 13, was recovered from a bathroom on the third floor of the madrasah around noon on August 3. His mother, Nazma Begum, later filed a case against the two teachers.
Police arrested the two accused from the madrasa around 10:00pm the same day. They were sent to jail the following day.
On August 5, Kadamtali thana Sub-Inspector Amzad Hossain, also the investigating officer in the case, sought five days’ remand for the accused. The court scheduled Thursday for the hearing in their presence.
During Thursday’s hearing, Advocate Harun ur Rashid Khan, appearing for the complainant, argued in favour of granting remand. Zakaria’s lawyer, Emdadul Alam, sought cancellation of the remand plea and bail for his client.
Zubayer’s lawyer claimed that he was a minor, prompting the court to defer the hearing on his remand.
The judge also sought Zakaria’s statement. He told the court that Naim went to the bathroom after the noon prayer call but did not return.
“Even after being called, he did not open the bathroom door. Senior students at the madrasah then opened the door and found him hanging by his shirt sleeve,” Zakaria said.
He said he was in Madanpur at the time and returned to the madrasa after receiving a phone call about the incident.
“When I arrived, his body was still warm. I called a doctor, who came and told us that the child was no longer alive,” he said.

item.description:
Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood on Thursday said that the country's ongoing energy crisis is expected to ease soon following the repair of a Floating Storage Regasification Unit (FSRU) and the arrival of LNG cargoes.
"The current gas shortage was triggered by an unexpected fire on an FSRU. While a major disaster was averted, the damage caused significant disruption to gas supplies and required specialized repairs by engineers from Britain and Singapore," he said.
The minister made the remarks as the chief guest at a discussion titled "Navigating Bangladesh's Energy Crisis: Immediate Priorities and the Path to a Sustainable Energy Future", organized by the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) in the city.
Iqbal Hassan Mahmood said a 72-hour total shutdown would be required for boiler maintenance after completion of the second phase of repairs, which could temporarily worsen the gas crisis.
However, the government has already procured LNG cargoes, which will be unloaded immediately after the FSRU becomes operational, he said, expressing hope that the move would significantly improve the current gas supply situation.
The minister also highlighted a significant change in the country's electricity demand pattern, saying peak demand now extends beyond midnight and recently reached 18,000 megawatts. He attributed much of the night-time demand to the charging of battery-run rickshaws.
Many of the charging points use illegal electricity connections, he said, adding that the ministry faces public resistance and even physical altercations when attempting to disconnect such connections.
Outlining the government's long-term roadmap, Iqbal Hasan Mahmud said three new FSRUs would be established by 2029 at Payra, Mongla and Hiron Point to strengthen LNG supply and improve distribution, particularly in the Khulna region.
The government is also planning to construct an undersea gas pipeline from Chattogram to Bakhrabad to overcome limitations in the existing pipeline network, he said.
The minister said the government is taking steps to strengthen Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company (BAPEX) after years of inadequate exploration, including ordering two new drilling rigs to intensify domestic gas exploration.
To provide immediate support to industries, he mentioned that the government has allowed a private company to transport gas from Bhola directly to factories.
He said Bangladesh is also holding discussions with Malaysia on introducing a containerized gas delivery system for industrial users, which could help supply gas without waiting for new pipelines to be constructed.
On energy-sector reforms, the minister said the government is moving away from the existing "single buyer system" to increase private-sector participation and strengthen energy security.
A new Fuel Oil Policy is being drafted to allow private-sector entities to import and distribute oil after consultations with stakeholders, he said.
Highlighting the recently adopted Solar Energy Policy, he said the government has introduced tax holidays and reduced duties on batteries and inverters to 5 percent to encourage the expansion of renewable energy.
Concluding his remarks, Iqbal Hasan Mahmood said the government is working on a war footing under the leadership of the prime minister to address the energy crisis and sought moral support from investors and the media in navigating the current challenges.

Presidential election: Nomination papers to be submitted Thursday
item.description:
Nomination papers must be submitted between 10am and 4pm on Thursday to run in the presidential election slated for August 20 next.
The ruling BNP has formally not declared its presidential candidate yet, while the opposition Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance has named LDP Chairman Col (retd) Oli Ahmed as its candidate.
However, both the ruling and opposition camps have collected nomination papers for their respective aspirants.
Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, who is serving as the returning officer of the presidential election, has already convened a meeting of the Members of Parliament (MPs) at the session chamber of the National Parliament on August 20 for voting in the presidential election in line with the Presidential Election Act, 1991.
According to the election schedule announced by the Election Commission on August 06 last, the nomination papers will be scrutinized on August 16 and the last date for withdrawal of candidature is August 18.
Voting will take place from 2:00pm to 5:00pm on August 20 in the session chamber of the National Parliament. A total of 349 MPs are voters in the presidential election. Now a parliamentary seat, Chittagong-4 constituency, remains vacant.
This will be the first presidential election in 35 years, which is going to involve more than one candidate. So, the voting is set to be held in the Presidential election after 1991.
The name of Local Government and Rural Development Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has already surfaced in the media as the BNP’s probable presidential candidate, but people are likely to wait till Thursday to formally know its candidate.
On July 24 last, Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned as President and Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad took charge as the acting president.
According to Article 123(2) of the Constitution, an election to fill the vacant office of the President must be held within 90 days of the post becoming vacant due to resignation.

item.title: Mango market buzzes in Chapainawabganj as season nears end
item.description:
Mango trading has gained momentum in Chapainawabganj as the season approaches its end, with large numbers of buyers and sellers gathering at major markets across the district.
At Kansat, the district’s largest mango market, trading of late-season and year-round varieties—including Ashwina, BARI-4, BARI-8, Gaurmati, Banana and Katimon—is continuing in full swing.
Thousands of maunds of mangoes are being traded at the market every day, while buyers and sellers remain active despite the season being in its final stage.
Speaking at Kansat market on Tuesday morning, mango grower Hasibul Hasan Babu of Binodpur union in Shibganj upazila said the season was almost over. He said he sold Ashwina mangoes for Tk 3,800 per maund that day, but the price was not satisfactory considering production costs.
Another grower, Monirul Islam of Durlabhpur union, sold BARI-4 mangoes for Tk 7,000 per maund. He said the variety used to fetch a much higher price several years ago. Although prices have improved somewhat recently, growers failed to receive their expected returns at the beginning of the season, he added.
Mango grower and media worker Farhad Ali brought Katimon mangoes to the market and sold them for Tk 6,000 per maund. While he was relatively satisfied with the price, he also expressed disappointment over the overall market situation this year.
Abdur Razzak, a trader involved in online mango trading for a long time, said prices had increased slightly toward the end of the season. However, the market remained unstable throughout the year. Traders like him still managed to make profits, he said.
Grower Abul Hasnat said Shibganj produces more mangoes than the district’s other four upazilas combined. He recalled that Fazli once accounted for nearly 80 percent of the orchards in the area.
In recent years, however, newer varieties such as Banana, Katimon, Amrapali and BARI-4 have increasingly entered the market around the time Fazli mangoes are harvested. As a result, demand for these newer varieties has risen during the late Fazli harvesting period, putting downward pressure on Fazli prices, he said.
Sentu Mia, a mango grower from the Maharajpur area of Sadar upazila, said he had been involved in mango cultivation for nearly two decades.
“Mango farming was profitable about 10 years ago, but growers have struggled to earn satisfactory returns in recent years,” he said. “Production costs have increased, but mango prices have not risen proportionately.”
Abu Taleb, president of the Shibganj Mango Aratdar Association, said the livelihoods of more than 100,000 people in Chapainawabganj were linked to the mango industry.
Production costs are rising every year, but growers are not receiving prices that adequately reflect those increases, he said.
He warned that the district’s mango industry is facing a serious threat and called for the development of mango processing industries, stronger agricultural research and the establishment of a full-fledged mango research institute to ensure the sector’s long-term sustainability.
Meanwhile, mangoes at Kansat, Rohanpur and other markets in the district are currently selling at around Tk 2,000-Tk 5,000 per maund for Ashwina, Tk 8,000-Tk 12,000 for BARI-4, Tk 5,000-Tk 7,000 for Gaurmati, Tk 5,000-Tk 8,000 for Katimon and Tk 12,000-Tk 15,000 for Banana varieties.
According to Atikul Islam, deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Chapainawabganj, mangoes were cultivated on 37,487 hectares of land in the district this season, with a production target of 458,912 metric tonnes.
He said supplies of several varieties, including Ashwina, Gaurmati, Banana and BARI-4, were continuing even as the mango season entered its final stage.
