Salman Shah family allegedly threatened after actor Don’s arrest
item.description:
The family of late actor Salman Shah has allegedly received death threats following the arrest of actor Ashraful Haque Don in the murder case involving the popular actor.
Mohammad Alamgir Kummkum, plaintiff in the case and Salman Shah’s maternal uncle, told reporters on Wednesday that Shahraan, Salman’s brother, had been threatened with death in a Facebook comment.
Kummkum showed journalists a screenshot of the alleged threat after appearing at a Dhaka court for Don’s bail hearing.
He said the threat was posted from a Facebook account named “Shakil Kibria” in the comments of a Facebook Live hosted by a Salman Shah fan named Mamun.
The screenshot showed the comment: “Mamun, tell Neela Chowdhury not to go too far regarding Salman’s death. Otherwise, we will kill Shahraan (Salman Shah’s brother) the way we killed Salman Shah.”
Kummkum said they would file a general diary (GD) with Ramna police over the threat, noting that the Salman Shah murder case was filed with the same police station.
Mamun, who was present at the court, said he was conducting the Facebook Live to call for a human chain by Salman Shah fans when the alleged threat appeared in the comments.
“The comment was later deleted while I was taking a screenshot,” he said.
“We, Salman fans, have been saying that he was murdered. Why are such threats coming after Don’s arrest? This should also be investigated,” Mamun said, urging authorities to bring everyone involved in the case to justice.
Don denied bail
Meanwhile, a Dhaka court rejected Don’s bail petition in the Salman Shah murder case.
On Wednesday afternoon, lawyers including M Faridul Islam and Tarikul Islam Jewel sought bail for Don before Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Ehsanul Islam.
Public Prosecutor Omar Faruk Faruqi opposed the petition, while the defence argued that there was no specific allegation against Don in the FIR or arrest warrant and that he was not involved in the alleged incident.
The court rejected the bail petition after hearing both sides.
Earlier, the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) took Don into custody after receiving information from immigration authorities as he was preparing to travel to Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.
He reportedly had a travel ban in connection with the Salman Shah murder case.
Murder case
Salman Shah died at his residence in Eskaton, Dhaka, on September 6, 1996. His death was initially recorded as a suicide, but a murder case was filed later.
The case has remained under investigation and legal scrutiny for decades.
On October 20, 2025, Kummkum filed a murder case with Ramna police on behalf of Salman’s mother, Neela Chowdhury, against 11 people.
The accused are Samira Haque, her mother Latifa Haque Lucy, businessman Aziz Mohammad Bhai, actor Ashraful Haque Don, David, Javed, Faruk, Ruby, Abdus Sattar, Saju and Rezvi Ahmed alias Farhad.
The latest death-threat allegation has renewed attention on the case, with Salman’s family and fans calling for an investigation to identify the person behind the threat and determine whether they have any connection to the murder case.

item.title: Bomb wrapped in pressure cooker recovered in Savar, defused
item.description:
Police recovered a bomb wrapped in a pressure cooker with scotch tape from a field in Savar’s Sadhapur area early Wednesday and later it was safely defused by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) bomb disposal unit.
Police and locals said the suspicious object was found inside a blue plastic drum at Ghora Mosque field around 1:30am.
The drum also contained some cloths and a copy of the Quran.
Savar Model Police Station Sub-Inspector Imran Hossain said they initially suspected that the object could be a bomb.
Locals removed the pressure cooker from the drum, placed it in the field and informed police.
Some residents said three unidentified people left the drum at the mosque field at night.
No one has been arrested in this connection yet.
A bomb disposal unit of DMP was informed and its members worked for about four hours before safely defusing the bomb in the afternoon, said the SI.
Earlier on July 30, police recovered another bomb concealed in a pressure cooker from an abandoned bag in front of Joyee General Store in Khejurbagan area of Ashulia.
The bomb disposal unit later defused it through a controlled explosion at a safe location.
Meanwhile, police on Tuesday night detained a youth named Arif Hossain with five crude bombs during a raid in Shyampur area of Hemayetpur in Savar.
On information provided by Arif, the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit later raided the ground floor of a four-storey building owned by Abdul Jalil and recovered nine more bomb-like objects, several leaflets and a large quantity of bomb-making materials and equipment.
Building owner Abdul Jalil and his daughter Ilma told journalists that a man identifying himself as Abbas Ali rented the apartment on Aug 2.
Savar Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Saiful Alam said a total of 14 bombs were recovered from Shyampur area.

item.title: Five arrested over Pallabi shooting linked to Tk15 lakh drug money dispute
item.description:
Five people, including a notorious drug trader, have been arrested in connection with a shooting incident in the capital’s Pallabi area over the sharing of Tk15 lakh earned from drug sales.
The arrestees are Hamid Khan alias Makhon, drug trader "Lengra" Rubel, Tanzid Ahmed alias Bappa, Parvez and Rabbi.
Police recovered a foreign-made pistol, two rounds of bullets, two magazines, 1,000 Yaba pills and two vehicles allegedly used in drug trading from their possession.
Additional Commissioner (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Md Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre on Wednesday afternoon.
He said the shooting took place in front of Emon’s tea stall at Mirpur Section-11 under Pallabi police station around 5:30pm on Aug 7.
Alamgir was shot in the abdomen and head, while a female passerby named Josna sustained a gunshot injury to her leg, he said.
Following a complaint filed by Alamgir’s wife, a case was filed with Pallabi Police Station on charges of attempted murder.
The DB Mirpur Division subsequently launched a shadow investigation.
With the help of video footage and information technology, investigators identified a Toyota Premio car used in the shooting and arrested its registered owner, Hamid Khan alias Makhon, from Pallabi.
During interrogation, Makhon told investigators that although the car was registered in his name, its actual owner is notorious drug trader "Lengra" Rubel.
Based on his information, Rubel’s associates Parvez and Rabbi were arrested from the Kalshi area.
Later, acting on information provided by Parvez and Rabbi, detectives arrested Lengra Rubel and Tanzid Ahmed alias Bappa in an area beside the embankment near Eastern Housing under Rupnagar Police Station.
A foreign-made pistol, two rounds of bullets and two magazines were recovered from them.
During preliminary interrogation, the arrestees said the shooting occurred following a dispute between Alamgir and Lengra Rubel and his associates over the sharing of Tk15 lakh earned from drug sales.
DB officials said Alamgir himself is a listed drug trader and faces several cases in Dhaka, but he is the victim in this case.
Responding to a question, Shafiqul Islam said anyone involved in a crime would be identified as a criminal regardless of their other identity and brought under the law.
He said Rubel faces several cases and investigators are looking into whether he invested money earned from drug trading in different places. If necessary, information will be sent to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for possible action under the Money Laundering Prevention Act.
The DB chief said preliminary interrogation also revealed that several other people, including Bappa, were in the vehicle during the shooting. Their identities are not being disclosed for the sake of investigation, and efforts are underway to arrest them.
Apart from the attempted murder case, separate cases under the Arms Act and Narcotics Control Act are being processed.
The arrestees may be taken on remand for further interrogation, while DB operations to arrest others involved in the incident are continuing, Shafiqul said.

Dhaka records ‘moderate’ air quality Wednesday morning
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 34th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 71 at 9:35am.
According to the AQI scale, the capital’s air quality was classified as ‘Moderate’, indicating that it generally poses little or no risk to the general population, though unusually sensitive individuals may experience some health concerns.
Malaysia’s Kuching topped the global pollution list with an AQI score of 223, followed by Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo with 179 and Baghdad in Iraq with 176.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, while 151 to 200 is classified as ‘unhealthy’. A reading between 201 and 300 is considered ‘very unhealthy’, and anything above 301 is categorized as ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Gunmen fire at 11-storey building overTk50L extortion demand in Ctg
item.description:
Gunmen fired two shots at the gate of an 11-storey building owned by an expatriate businessman in Chittagong Hamzarbagh area on Monday night, allegedly after a Tk50 lakh extortion demand went unmet.
The incident took place around 11pm, sparking panic among residents.
The building, Runa Tower, is owned by Mohammad Yusuf, whose two sons are expatriate businessmen. Their ancestral home is in Fatikchhari. Yusuf is the father-in-law of Azizur Rahman Aziz, general secretary of the Chittagong city unit of the banned Awami League-affiliated Swechchhasebak League. Aziz was arrested two days after the fall of the Awami League government on August 5, 2024, and remains in jail.
Building security guard Mohammad Alamgir Hossain said there was no electricity at the time.
“Two young men wearing pants and shirts suddenly arrived and asked us to close the gate. They then fired two shots at the gate before walking away. Hearing the gunshots, local residents gathered, and police later arrived,” he said.
Yusuf said his son Shawkat received a voice message on WhatsApp from a foreign number around noon on Monday, giving him one hour to pay Tk50 lakh.
According to Yusuf, the message claimed the senders knew where his children lived and worked and had details about their properties. They threatened to kill them if the money was not paid within the stipulated time.
Panchlaish police station Officer-in-Charge Jahedul Islam said gunmen fired at the building gate after the extortion demand was not met.
“We are working to identify and arrest those involved. No case has been filed yet,” he said.
The incident comes amid a series of alleged extortion-related attacks in Chittagong.
On July 13, associates of alleged criminal Mobarak Hossain Emon were accused of attacking and vandalising a businessman’s under-construction building in the Bor Dighirpar area of South Pahartali Ward after he allegedly refused to pay Tk20 lakh in extortion. A case was filed over the incident, followed by a demand for Tk50 lakh.
Earlier, on June 13, Emon’s associates were also accused of attacking and vandalising internet service provider DDN on Bakalia Access Road over an alleged demand for Tk2 crore.
Following the incidents, locals held human chains and press conferences demanding an end to extortion and Emon’s arrest.
Emon allegedly became increasingly involved in extortion and other criminal activities after August 5, 2024. He was arrested in Jessore on July 29 while allegedly attempting to flee to India and is currently on a 10-day remand.

item.title: Bangladesh-China pledge to work together on water resources management
item.description:
Bangladesh and China expressed their commitment to working together on water resources management.
The two sides made the commitment as Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen paid a courtesy call on Water Resources Minister Md Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee at his Secretariat office in the capital on Tuesday.
State Minister for Water Resources Forhad Hossain Azad was also present.
Anee said China and Bangladesh are long-standing and time-tested friends, and that the two countries maintain strong bilateral relations. He called for cooperation between the two countries in exchanging knowledge and experience in water resources management, education, technological cooperation, professional capacity development, and research.
Yao Wen said that China is interested in working with Bangladesh to ensure the conservation of water resources and maintain environmental balance.
He said China wants to stand by Bangladesh in addressing issues related to water resources management, floods, droughts, waterlogging, and river erosion.
Water Resources Secretary Dr AKM Shahabuddin and Chinese Embassy’s Economic and Commercial Counsellor Song Yang were present during the meeting.

item.title: Fishing resumes in Kaptai Lake after 3.5-month ban
item.description:
Fishing has resumed in Kaptai Lake after a three-and-a-half-month ban, bringing fishermen, traders and transport workers back to the lake and its busy landing centres.
The ban on fishing, fish transportation and marketing ended at midnight on Monday. From early Tuesday, motorised boats began arriving at the Kaptai fish landing centre with catches from different parts of the lake, including Bagaichhari, Langadu, Barkal and Bilaichhari.
The first boats reached the centre around 6:30am, carrying drums filled with kachki, chapila, tengra, ayir, baim, bacha, kaligunia and pabda.
The landing centre quickly became busy as fishermen unloaded their catches and traders prepared the fish for shipment. After paying the required duties, traders packed the fish in ice and loaded them onto trucks bound for Chattogram, Dhaka and northern districts.
A total of 28,866kg of fish were landed at the Kaptai centre between 6:30am and 1pm on Tuesday, said Jasim Uddin, head of the Kaptai Fisheries Development Sub-centre. The government collected Tk6.20 lakh in revenue from the day's catch.
At Rangamati Fisheries Ghat, traders said the first day's catch was dominated by smaller fish.
Md Shahjahan said adverse weather on Monday had prevented many fishermen from casting their nets, making it too early to assess the season's overall catch.
“Fish are generally smaller at the beginning of the season. Larger fish are usually caught later,” he said.
Commander Mohammad Foyez Al Karim, manager of the Kaptai Lake Fisheries Development and Marketing Centre, said a substantial quantity of fish had reached the landing centre by noon.
He said traders might be concerned about the relatively small size of chapila but expected the fish to grow larger within the next 10 to 15 days.
Foyez said the fish production target for the 2025-26 fiscal year was 8,500 tonnes, but actual production reached 10,000 tonnes, generating Tk22.60 crore in revenue.
The district administration initially imposed this year's fishing ban from April 25 to July 31 to allow fish to breed and replenish stocks. The ban was later extended by 10 days until midnight on August 10.
The reopening has brought relief to thousands of people whose livelihoods depend on the lake, while traders, transport workers and others are expecting increased economic activity.
Kaptai Lake, Bangladesh's largest artificial reservoir, is a major source of fish and hydropower and an important water transport and tourism route. Its resources are closely linked to the economy and livelihoods of people across Rangamati.

item.title: Dhaka-Gopalganj train service starts
item.description:
For Gopalganj residents who have waited years for a direct train to the capital, marked the end of a long journey — but the new service has arrived with a catch: its evening schedule.
The Abhijatri Commuter made its first trip from Dhaka to Gopalganj on Monday, opening a direct rail link between the district and the capital through the Padma Bridge rail route.
The train left Kamalapur Railway Station at 3:30pm and reached Gopalganj at 7:10pm. After a brief reception at Gopalganj Railway Station, it departed for Dhaka at 8:05pm.
The service will run six days a week, except Saturday, with 609 seats. The fare from Gopalganj to Dhaka has been set at Tk145, while the journey takes around three and a half hours.
Under the regular schedule, the train will leave Dhaka at 3:30pm and reach Gopalganj at 6:45pm. It will leave Gopalganj at 7:15pm and reach Dhaka around 10:30pm, stopping at nine stations.
The launch drew crowds to Gopalganj Railway Station, where residents gathered to witness a rail connection they had been waiting years for.
For many, the low-cost service is expected to ease travel to Dhaka for education, healthcare, business and employment. But passengers say the evening schedule limits its usefulness, particularly for students, traders and women.
Md Zakir Hossain of Khatia Garh Union in Gopalganj Sadar travelled to Dhaka with his wife on the inaugural train.
“We are extremely happy and excited that train service from Gopalganj to Dhaka has finally started after such a long wait,” he said.
But he urged the authorities to introduce a morning service.
“This is not just my demand; it is the long-standing expectation of the people of Gopalganj,” Hossain said.
Shabnur Khanom, a third-year honours student at Gopalganj Government College, said the train would significantly reduce travel costs for students.
“We often have to travel to Dhaka for job examinations and other purposes. A bus journey costs around Tk500, while the train fare is only Tk145,” she said.
She said a morning service would allow students to reach Dhaka earlier and reduce the risk of missing examinations because of traffic congestion.
For fish trader Motaleb Fakir, the timing is an even bigger concern.
“If the train left Gopalganj around 7am, we could take fish and other fresh produce to Dhaka and return the same day,” he said, adding that an evening service could force traders to stay overnight in Dhaka and incur additional costs.
Gopalganj Railway Station Master Ratna Baidya said the 609-seat service would operate six days a week and provide an affordable travel option for people heading to Dhaka.
The railway project connecting Gopalganj was taken up in 2010. The Rajbari-Gopalganj-Tungipara railway line was inaugurated in November 2018 after construction and renovation work costing around Tk2,110 crore.
Despite the railway infrastructure, Gopalganj had no direct passenger train to Dhaka.
That changed after the Dhaka-Bhanga railway line opened in December 2024 under the Padma Bridge Rail Link Project, creating the opportunity for a direct connection.
With Monday’s launch of the Abhijatri Commuter, Gopalganj has finally gained that long-awaited link — though passengers are already asking for a timetable that works better for them.

item.title: Jute cultivation exceeds target in Khulna region
item.description:
Jute cultivation in Khulna agricultural region has exceeded the seasonal target, with favourable weather, higher prices and growing demand for eco-friendly products encouraging farmers to expand the crop.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), farmers in Khulna, Bagerhat, Narail and Satkhira have cultivated jute on 38,361 hectares this year, surpassing the target of 38,287 hectares.
With the peak harvesting season now underway, farmers across the region are busy harvesting jute, while canals, beels, rivers and ponds have turned into busy sites for retting, fibre extraction and drying.
So far, farmers have harvested jute from 20,083 hectares, producing around 90,535 tonnes of fibre — about 51.9% of the region’s cultivated area.
During a recent visit to Terokhada upazila in Khulna, hundreds of men and women were seen working along the Atharobeki River and nearby beels in Baoisona and Kolabaria villages.
Women’s participation in post-harvest processing was particularly noticeable. Many women separate fibre from retted jute without entering the water, often taking jute sticks instead of cash as payment.
“I extract jute fibre in exchange for keeping the jute sticks,” said Jharna Begum of Kolabaria.
Tohura Banu, a first-year student at Terokhada College, said she helps her family process jute during college holidays.
“I enjoy the work, and it also helps my family,” she said.
Mahmud Gazi, who was working in the Atharobeki River, said a team of 15 labourers earns around Tk800 a day, while some workers are paid Tk5 per bundle.
Across the region, freshly extracted fibres can be seen drying on bamboo frames, bridge railings and around homesteads, while piles of jute sticks line village roads.
Farmers said favourable rainfall has made retting easier this year.
Mahtab Hossain of Baoisona village, who cultivated jute on three bighas, said heavy rainfall during Ashar and Sraban filled nearby water bodies, reducing the cost of transporting jute to retting sites.
However, frequent rain and limited sunshine have made drying the fibre difficult, he said.
Jute is also proving useful in maintaining the productivity of farmland between major crop seasons.
Soumen Bairagi of Golna village in Dumuria said farmers can grow jute between the wheat or pulse harvest and Aman rice cultivation, preventing land from remaining fallow.
“Early sowing in Chaitra also allows farmers to harvest jute in time for Aman transplantation,” he said.
Farmers also cited better prices and expanding domestic and international markets as key reasons behind the renewed interest in jute.
Trading of the new season’s jute has already begun at major markets in Khulna, including Khalishpur, Daulatpur and Khanjahan Ali.
Farmer Anser Ali said he sold freshly harvested jute for Tk3,700 per maund at Daulatpur market.
Veteran jute trader Fazlu Sharif, former vice-president of the Bangladesh Jute Association, said he expected prices to remain profitable for farmers and traders.
Jute is currently selling for Tk3,500-Tk4,500 per maund, with prices expected to rise further as marketing gains momentum.
Md Rafiqul Islam, additional director of the Khulna Agriculture Region, said average production currently stands at around 8.5 maunds per bigha and is expected to increase as harvesting continues.
“Abundant rainfall this season created favourable conditions for jute retting,” he said.
He attributed the rise in cultivation partly to increasing global demand for environmentally friendly products, saying higher prices have encouraged farmers to expand the crop.
The government has also provided incentives, while the agriculture department is supporting farmers through training and modern production technologies, he added.

item.title: Health officials report 756 fresh cases of dengue infection overnight
item.description:
Health officials on Tuesday said they recorded 756 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts in the past 24 hours.
“During the period, (of the 756) 80 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 89 in Chittagong division, 158 in Dhaka division, 106 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 110 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 101 in Khulna division, 27 in Mymensingh division, 63 in Rajshahi division, 17 in Rangpur division and five in Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaught, Bangladesh this year has witnessed so far 61 deaths while the disease inflicted 20,727.
Last year, dengue claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, dengue claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: Home minister urges US businesses to boost investment in Bangladesh
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Tuesday urged US businesses to increase investment in Bangladesh, assuring them of a business-friendly environment and comprehensive security for foreign investors.
The minister made the call when a high-level delegation from the US-Bangladesh Business Council (USBBC), led by its President and US Chamber of Commerce Senior Vice President for South Asia Atul Keshap, met with him at the conference room of the Home Ministry at the Bangladesh Secretariat this afternoon.
During the meeting, they discussed various issues of bilateral interest, including ways to increase bilateral trade and investment between Bangladesh and the United States, as well as energy and security cooperation, according to a ministry press release.
The minister reiterated the government's strong commitment to creating an investment-friendly environment in Bangladesh and ensuring overall security for foreign investors.
He said Bangladesh currently offers ample opportunities for foreign direct investment (FDI), while the government has ensured a tariff-friendly environment for the convenience of investors.
Welcoming increased US investment in Bangladesh, the minister said the government has taken necessary legal and administrative measures to launch a one-stop service called "Invest Bangladesh" to bring the investment process under one umbrella and make operations easier.
He said administrative and legal facilities in this regard have been streamlined over the past five to six months.
The government is also examining various proposals for setting up LNG terminals at strategically important locations in the country, which would help diversify the energy sector and enhance overall national security, he said.
The minister further said major opportunities are being created for investment in food grain and energy supply, ranging from government-to-government (G2G) arrangements to private-sector investment.
He said initiatives have also been taken to introduce digital security measures, the "Safe City" project under smart policing, "Integrated Border Management" for border security and e-visa facilities to strengthen national security and technological protection.
Atul Keshap said major US companies have been successfully operating in Bangladesh for several decades and are currently among the country's major investors.
Highlighting Bangladesh's immense potential, he said the country's economy is expected to reach $1 trillion by 2034.
To achieve this target, he said, developing technical and managerial capacity, along with increasing GDP growth and tax productivity, is crucial.
He also discussed how US companies could provide comprehensive support and become partners of the Bangladesh government in the country's development process.
A 16-member delegation of business leaders from the US-Bangladesh Business Council, led by Atul Keshap, and senior officials of the Home Ministry attended the meeting.

item.title: JU English dept holds workshop on visual thinking, literary theory
item.description:
The Department of English at Jahangirnagar University (JU) held a workshop on visual thinking and idea generation on August 2, introducing MA students to creative approaches to understanding and applying contemporary literary and cultural theories.
Titled “Visual Thinking and Idea Generation,” the workshop was held from 11:30am to 1pm at the department as part of the MA course LECS 502: Contemporary Critical Theories and Pedagogies (Critical Humanities).
Cartoonist and illustrator Eeha Nawar attended the session as the guest speaker.
The four-credit core course introduces students to a range of theoretical frameworks, including Affect Theory, Ethical Criticism, Trauma and Testimonial Criticism, Medical Humanities, Posthumanism, Ecocriticism, Cognitive Literary Criticism and Digital Humanities.
During the workshop, Nawar demonstrated how visual arts, media texts and editorial cartoons can be used alongside literary theories to explore contemporary cultural and social issues.
She said literary theory was not confined to written texts and discussed how visual thinking could offer alternative ways of approaching complex theoretical concepts.
“Learn, study and understand the other side of the story. It helps develop critical thinking and contributes to building a strong character,” Nawar said.
Students participating in the workshop explored different methods of visualising ideas through art, including mind mapping, selecting visual elements and developing concepts across different media.
The session also covered the use of digital installations, graphic texts, cartoons and doodles as tools for developing and communicating ideas.
The workshop concluded with an interactive question-and-answer session, during which students discussed ways of applying visual media and digital humanities approaches to their course materials.
Other students from the department also attended the session.

item.title: Chief Whip: MPs bound by party line in presidential election
item.description:
Chief Whip of Parliament Nurul Islam Moni on Tuesday said members of parliament will not be able to vote in the presidential election, slated for August 20, against their party's decision as Article 70 of the Constitution remains unchanged.
“As Article 70 of the Constitution has not been amended, it will remain effective. No one will be able to vote beyond the party's decision. If anyone does so, their membership of Parliament will be cancelled,” he said at a press briefing at the Media Centre of Parliament after the 2026 presidential election preparatory meeting held at the Cabinet Room of Parliament.
Acting Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal chaired the preparatory meeting. Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam and Whips Md G K Gouse, Rakibul Islam Bakul, Mia Nuruddin Ahmed Apu, Md Akhtaruzzaman Mia and A B M Ashraf Uddin Nizan also attended the meeting.
Speaking at the meeting, Acting Speaker Kayser Kamal said the state structure must be freed from fascism in all spheres.
“The 2026 presidential election is going to be held at a historic moment in building a fascism-free Bangladesh,” he said.
During the meeting, all necessary preparations, including the use of the Jatiya Sangsad chamber for holding the 2026 presidential election, all necessary logistical support and ensuring the attendance of Members of Parliament, were discussed.
The meeting also instructed completing all necessary preparations and providing logistical support for the election.
According to the election schedule announced by the Election Commission, the 2026 presidential election will be held in the Parliament chamber on Thursday, August 20.
The Chief Election Commissioner will conduct the election as the return officer in line with the Presidential Election Act, 1991. EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed, Parliament Secretary Golam Sorwar Bhuiyan and other senior officials concerned of the Parliament Secretariat were present at the meeting.
At the press conference, Chief Whip Nurul Islam said the BNP's candidate for the presidential election has not yet been finalised. “The party has entrusted the Prime Minister with the responsibility of finalising the candidate. He will announce the candidate,” he said.
He said the opposition has already nominated a candidate and the meeting was held to ensure a fair election.
“According to the election schedule, voting will be held in the Parliament chamber from 2pm to 5pm on August 20,” he said. Nurul Islam said the voting will take place inside Parliament and a ballot box will be placed there. Members of Parliament will cast their votes according to their division and seat number, he added.
He said preparations would be made to declare the result before the scheduled closing time if all 349 votes are cast within the first hour of voting. If it is found that one vote remains, it will wait until 5pm. After 5pm, the result will be announced, he said. The Chief Whip said the voting of the (Acting) President, Leader of the House, Leader of the Opposition and (Acting) Speaker would be broadcast live. After voting is completed, the counting of votes and the process leading to the declaration of the result may also be broadcast live, he said.
Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam said the presidential election should have been held in accordance with the “July Charter” to intensify acceptance and dignity of an elected president.
As the election was being held anyway, the opposition did not want to allow it to take place without a contest, he said.

item.title: Five arrested over attempted murder of BNP activist in Pallabi
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Mirpur division has arrested five people, including the prime accused Rubel and Bappa alias Shakil, in connection with the attempted murder of BNP activist Alamgir Hossain in the capital’s Pallabi.
The other arrestees are: Hamidur alias Makhon, Parvez and Rabbi.
Mohammad Rakib Khan, deputy commissioner of the DB’s Mirpur division, said the five were arrested during raids in different areas of Savar, Gazipur and Kushtia on Monday.
Police recovered a pistol, two rounds of ammunition, two magazines, a private car allegedly used in the attack and a Volkswagen from their possession. They also recovered 1,000 yaba tablets, he said.
According to Rakib Khan, none of the suspects remained in Dhaka after the shooting. One was first arrested in Gazipur, while the others were later detained in Aminbazar, Savar and Kushtia.
The shooting took place at around 5:45pm last Friday when assailants got out of a private car and opened fire at Alamgir Hossain, 45, in Pallabi. A passerby, Jotsna, was also hit by a bullet.
Alamgir is undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital, while Jotsna was treated at Kurmitola General Hospital and has since returned home.
Alamgir’s wife filed a case with Pallabi Police Station over the attack, naming Mohammad Rubel as the prime accused.

item.title: Energy minister: Investment-friendly policy adopted for energy sector
item.description:
Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood, MP, on Tuesday said the government has adopted an investment-friendly policy to increase private investment in the energy and power sectors.
He also observed that creating opportunities to earn money alone would not be enough for sustainable development of the country's industries and economy; rather, sustainable infrastructure also needs to be developed.
The minister made the remark while addressing as the chief guest a seminar titled “Crisis in the Energy Sector: Prospects and Ways Forward” organized by the Forum for Energy Reporters Bangladesh (FERB) at Dhaka Club.
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit, MP, attended the seminar as the special guest.
Former professor of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology and energy expert Dr Ijaz Hossain presented the keynote paper.
Iqbal Hassan Mahmood said the issue was being considered seriously so that an accident at any single LNG facility would not have a negative impact on industries across the country.
Discussions are also underway with the relevant parties on alternative arrangements and timing to address possible crises in LNG supply, he said.
He said the government remained alert to ensure that industries do not suffer, adding that discussions are underway with industrial entrepreneurs, intellectuals and experts to find ways to address the current crisis in the energy sector.
Iqbal Hasan Mahmood also referred to the meetings of the prime minister with industrial entrepreneurs within a short time after assuming office.
Cautioning against setting up coal-fired power plants, he said developed countries have reservations about coal-based power generation. Even in many cases, financing for such projects has been stopped. "So, we have to move forward very cautiously regarding these power stations," he said.
Saying that the government has taken an aggressive plan for solar power generation, the minister mentioned a new policy had been formulated within just two months. Various facilities have been kept in the policy to make it investment-friendly, including a five-year tax holiday, he added.
He said the government would implement the facilities highlighted in the policy to stop harassment of investors in the solar power sector.
The minister said: “It is our desire, and I think it is possible that we can achieve our target of 10,000 megawatts."
He said importance was being given to the OPEX model, particularly in solar power generation, and there is a plan to expand rooftop solar power gradually across the country, starting from Dhaka city.
Private investment would be encouraged instead of government investment in this regard, he said, adding that discussions had already been held with the two administrations of the Dhaka City Corporation.
He continued that an initiative is being taken to identify area-based sites and invite investors.
The minister said investors would be able to install rooftop solar power facilities, like cable television or Wi-Fi (internet) businesses, and collect bills from customers. Therefore, there is no need to depend on the government for everything, he added.
The minister also spoke of a partnership model for the use of government land in large solar power projects, under which the government could become a partner in the investment by providing land.
He said the government could provide land for the project and the value of that land could be included as the government's share within the investment structure. "I think there can be no better proposal than this," he said.
Informing about plans to further involve the private sector in importing fuel oil, the minister said unnecessary panic had been created in the country over fuel oil supplies in recent times centring on the conflict in the Middle East.
He said long queues were formed at petrol pumps in panic despite having adequate stock. Later, incidents of black-market trading and online-based fuel sales were also seen.
He said discussions had been held with the prime minister about allowing the private sector to import fuel oil following the situation.
The minister said allowing the private sector to operate alongside the government system would increase competition in the market and strengthen the supply system.
"Let there be one government [operator] and another private one, as in India," he said.
Rejecting allegations that the fuel import policy was being formulated to benefit a particular company, the minister said if it was a general law or policy, it would not be for any particular company and would apply equally to all.
"The notion that we are doing this to give it to a particular company is not correct," he said.
Urging against spreading confusion or attempts to worsen the crisis in the energy sector for political purposes, the minister said everyone would have to play a responsible role in the national interest.
He assured that investment proposals submitted by the private sector would be approved quickly if they were attractive and helpful to the industry.
Iqbal Hasan Mahmood said: "If the proposal is attractive and helpful for our industry, certainly we will not waste any time."
He further said the government would review private sector proposals seriously. After receiving a proposal, necessary approvals would be arranged following discussions and scrutiny with the concerned parties.

item.title: DMP files 915 cases against black smoke-emitting vehicles in July
item.description:
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Traffic Division filed 915 cases against vehicles emitting excessive black smoke during drives across the capital in July.
The DMP’s Media and Public Relations Division confirmed the matter.
According to DMP Traffic Division sources, regular drives are being conducted to curb environmental pollution and prevent vehicles from emitting excessive black smoke on the roads.
As part of the ongoing campaign, traffic police conducted drives in various parts of the capital throughout July and filed the cases against vehicles found emitting black smoke.
Of the 915 cases, 34 were filed by the Ramna Traffic Division, 354 by Motijheel, four by Lalbagh, 172 by Wari, 131 by Tejgaon, 36 by Mirpur, 128 by Uttara and 56 by Gulshan.
The Motijheel division recorded the highest number of cases, with 354, while Lalbagh recorded the lowest, with four.
The DMP said drives against black smoke-emitting vehicles and legal action against violators would continue as part of its efforts to reduce air pollution.
